title: Screaming Frog 24 MCP Tool Mapping Contract v1.0
description: Meta-schema for the Screaming Frog 24 native MCP integration contract (v1.8 §SF). Validates a use-case registry document that maps 6 canonical SF MCP use-cases to MCP tool calls, staging tables, projection modes, cache policy, and Tier 1/2 report bundles. D-SF-01: HTTP transport (only HTTP MCP in registry currently). D-SF-08: separate mapping file (NOT embedded in mcp-tool-registry) — mirrors gsc-tool-mapping + dataforseo-endpoint-mapping + scrapling-output-mapping pattern. The orchestrator (skills/ingestion/sf-crawl-orchestrator, Phase 3) reads this registry to plan the 24-report Tier 1+2 loop. URL normalization is inherited from the global pipeline — Tier 1 reports that contain url-bearing rows write both url_original and url_normalized at projection time (handled by existing sf-import skill, not the orchestrator). Canonical use-case keys and mcp_tool names are carried in enums as the single source of truth.

mcp_server_name.description: MCP server short name carrying these tools; must match the key used in .mcp.json + mcp-tool-registry.json (D-SF-02 short name 'sf', 3 chars matches gsc 3-char convention).

url_normalization.description: Inherited from global pipeline. The orchestrator does not normalize URLs directly — it writes raw CSV files to sf-exports/{date}/raw/ and hands off to the existing sf-import skill, which applies project.config.url_policy at projection time. Recorded here for cross-MCP contract symmetry.

use_cases.description: The 6 canonical SF MCP use-cases. Keys are fixed vocabulary; values conform to #/definitions/useCase.

useCaseKey.description: Canonical SF MCP use-case keys. crawl_trigger initiates a new crawl; crawl_progress_poll watches in-flight; report_export_inline returns CSV-as-string in MCP response (small reports); report_export_save writes CSV to allowed_directory (large reports, default for Tier 1/2 loop); crawl_list enumerates active crawl ids; allowed_dir_discovery probes the SF GUI for runtime base directory (pre-flight check).

sfMcpTool.description: SF MCP tool identifier in the mcp-tool-registry.json naming convention `{server_key}__{native_tool_name_verbatim}`. Post-Phase-1 Fix Worker correction (Q-PHASE-1-POLISH-01): native SF 24 MCP tools carry the `sf_` prefix verbatim (sf_crawl, sf_crawl_progress, ...), so the registry-side identifier is `sf__sf_<name>` (server_key + double underscore + verbatim native name). The original 'sf__<verb>' shorthand was an analogy error; corrected here post v1.8 Phase 1 Fix Worker round. The 5 entries are the production tool surface advertised by SF 24's native MCP server at port 11435.

projectionMode.description: Mirrors staging-to-excel-map projection_mode enum. Null means the orchestrator writes a raw file and hands off to sf-import (no direct Excel projection from the orchestrator).

inputField.description: One input parameter; either declares a static type (with optional format/default/enum/const) or binds to a project.config source path. Mirrors gsc-tool-mapping inputField shape exactly for cross-MCP symmetry.

source.description: Dot-path into project.config.* for runtime binding (e.g. project.config.sf.mcp.url, project.config.sf.mcp.allowed_directory).

output_fields.description: Canonical staging columns preserved from the MCP response (pre-projection). For report_export_save the response carries metadata (file path, row count, truncated flag); the actual report rows land on disk and are read by sf-import.

staging_table.description: SQLite staging table (§6.2). Convention: sf_*. For orchestrator-level meta-tracking (e.g. sf_crawl_runs); the actual report data lands in sf-export-mapping-driven tables via sf-import.

oneOf.description: Orchestrator-level use-cases never write Excel directly (handoff to sf-import).

tier.description: Which sf-required-reports tier this use-case feeds. Tier 1 = 14 mandatory reports; Tier 2 = 10 recommended; Tier 3 = optional (Q-SF-MCP-10 default OFF). Orchestrator-only use-cases (crawl_trigger, crawl_list, allowed_dir_discovery) are tagged 'meta' — they don't map to a tier.
